sources_considered.why: Reprint of Figure's press release on its $39B valuation, showing the level of hype and investment.
Reports the WSJ hands-on test of 1X NEO, the most prominent 2025 home humanoid, and its teleoperation.
Reports Tesla's 2025 Optimus production halt over hand design, citing The Information.
Expert context on 2025 humanoid hype. Marcus cites Brooks, but Brooks is not the speaker.

evidence_items.publisher: Figure (press release reprinted by Venture Capital Access Online)

receipt.public_excerpt: Figure, the AI robotics company developing autonomous general-purpose humanoid robots, today announced it has exceeded more than $1 billion in committed capital through its Series C financing round, at a post-money valuation of $39 billion.

evidence_items.explanation: A $39 billion valuation for a humanoid startup in 2025 shows the high level of hype and investment the claim predicted.

evidence_items.locator: section 'How much of it is real?'

receipt.public_excerpt: In Joanna Stern’s video, 100% of the work being done was completely teleoperated through Expert Mode

evidence_items.explanation: The most prominent 2025 home humanoid, 1X NEO, opened for preorders with delivery in 2026. In the WSJ hands-on test, all the work was done by a remote human operator. That is far from an autonomous Rosie.

receipt.public_excerpt: Tesla is scaling back plans to produce thousands of Optimus robots this year due to issues with their hand design.

evidence_items.explanation: Tesla's heavily promoted Optimus was not released in 2025 and had production paused over hand-design problems.

receipt.public_excerpt: Recently a new generation has stumbled upon the idea of building humanoid robots and you may have noticed just a little bit of hype about it.

evidence_items.explanation: A leading roboticist's September 2025 essay remarks wryly on the hype around humanoids. This is context only; Brooks holds the same view as Marcus.

unresolved_gaps: No full survey of every humanoid released in 2025, including Chinese makers such as Unitree, was done. None of the reviewed sources suggests any was Rosie-level.
'Situational awareness and cognitive flexibility' were not measured directly by any benchmark.
